newsitem.title: GREECE: Drachma firms vs ecu, bonds flat, forwards up.
newsitem.headline: Drachma firms vs ecu, bonds flat, forwards up.

text.p: The drachma was registering fresh gains against the ecu around mid-session, trading around 308.25/30, after opening at 308.50/55, and dealers said a firmer dollar could give the drachma another boost.
"The drachma is up against the ecu and a firmer dollar vis-a-vis the mark could push it higher," a forex dealer at a foreign bank said.

News of a lower-than-expected German M3 money supply growth increased the likelihood that Buba would not raise its rates on Thursday, pushing dollar/mark up to test the 1.84 level briefly before receding to stabilise below it.
Forex forwards were also firmer from one-week to-three month periods on funding for the upcoming auction of FRNs, dealers said. Depos were also up in short tenors.
The finance ministry said on Monday that it would seek to raise 100 billion drachmas via its FRN auction on August 21.
Bonds were idling in thin trading with prices holding Monday levels.
"Many traders are away on vacation and volumes are thin with prices going through a period of consolidation," said a senior bond dealer.
The dealer said the T-bill rate cuts announced by the finance ministry on Monday would not help the treasury's efforts to lower in debt servicing costs in the long-run.
The treasury said it would slash three-, six- and 12-month T-bill rates by 10 basis points to 8.4 percent, 8.7 percent and 9.5 percent effective today.
It will also offer 12-month T-bills to the public on August 20.
"I can understand the motive behind the rate cuts but I do not think it will help in the long-run because outstanding FRNs will become less attractive," the dealer said.
Greek floaters are refixed, using the 12-month T-bill rate.
The 10-year bond was trading around 94.65 at mid-session, with the spread over Bunds standing at 403 basis points.
The market was quoted at 156.70/73 from Monday's 157.195 fix, the dollar at 287.51/61 from 285.470 and the ecu at 308.16/21 from 308.600.
